newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: FORECAST - Irish bourse seen up 7.5pct by yr-end - NCB.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Irish bourse seen up 7.5pct by yr-end - NCB.

text.p: The Irish stock market index is expected to rise by 7.5 percent to 3,250 by the end of the year, with an increase to 3050 by mid-year, NCB Stockbrokers said in a note on Wednesday.
The Irish ISEQ index of shares was trading at 3,020 by 1330 GMT on Wednesday, up just under 24 points on the day on the back of Wall Street's recent strong rally.
NCB said developments in international markets will restrict the pace of growth in share prices over the next few months but expected stronger growth in the second half of the year.
"We expect the U.S. Fed to raise interest rates by another 25-50 basis points and this will hold back the U.S. equity market," NCB said.
It said election uncertainty will weigh on the UK market but the underlying bias will be upwards.
The second half of the year will see a stronger performance with the Irish market benefiting from a better international environment as well as domestic robustness, it said.
Once the U.S. completes its monetary policy tightening, which it did not expect to be aggressive, NCB said it expected the U.S. equity market to progress from current levels.
It expected the UK market to pick up also in the second half, despite a likely rise in interest rates.

"We expect the Irish construction sector to record another year of very strong growth in 1997," NCB said. "Output is forecast to increase by 12 percent, bringing output levels above the previous peak level of the early 1980s."
In 1998, output growth should moderate but a forecast expansion of five percent would still be strong in European terms, it said.
NCB said growth in 1997 will be fuelled by strong growth in new housing - in turn driven by favourable demographic influences - and by growth in public construction.
